playwright.name: mcp_playwright_browser_close
playwright.description: [playwright] Close the page

playwright.name: mcp_playwright_browser_resize
playwright.description: [playwright] Resize the browser window

playwright.name: mcp_playwright_browser_console_messages
playwright.description: [playwright] Returns all console messages

level.description: Level of the console messages to return. Each level includes the messages of more severe levels. Defaults to "info".

all.description: Return all console messages since the beginning of the session, not just since the last navigation. Defaults to false.

filename.description: File name to save the console messages to. Relative file names are resolved against the workspace root. If not provided, messages are returned as text.

playwright.name: mcp_playwright_browser_handle_dialog
playwright.description: [playwright] Handle a dialog

promptText.description: The text of the prompt in case of a prompt dialog.

playwright.name: mcp_playwright_browser_emulate_media
playwright.description: [playwright] Emulate CSS media features for the page, for example switch between the light and dark color scheme. Omitted parameters are left unchanged; null clears an override.

media.description: Changes the CSS media type of the page

playwright.name: mcp_playwright_browser_evaluate
playwright.description: [playwright] Evaluate JavaScript expression on page or element

element.description: Human-readable element description used to obtain permission to interact with the element

target.description: Exact target element reference from the page snapshot, or a unique element selector

function.description: () => { /* code */ } or (element) => { /* code */ } when element is provided

filename.description: File name to save the result to. Relative file names are resolved against the workspace root. If not provided, result is returned as text.

playwright.name: mcp_playwright_browser_file_upload
playwright.description: [playwright] Upload one or multiple files

paths.description: The absolute paths to the files to upload. Can be single file or multiple files. If omitted, file chooser is cancelled.

playwright.name: mcp_playwright_browser_drop
playwright.description: [playwright] Drop files or MIME-typed data onto an element, as if dragged from outside the page. At least one of "paths" or "data" must be provided.

element.description: Human-readable element description used to obtain permission to interact with the element

target.description: Exact target element reference from the page snapshot, or a unique element selector

paths.description: Absolute paths to files to drop onto the element.

data.description: Data to drop, as a map of MIME type to string value (e.g. {"text/plain": "hello", "text/uri-list": "https://example.com"}).

playwright.name: mcp_playwright_browser_find
playwright.description: [playwright] Search the accessibility snapshot of the current page for text or a regular expression. Returns matching snapshot nodes with a few lines of surrounding context (like search snippets), each shown under its path from the root of the tree, which is cheaper than capturing the whole snapshot when you only need to locate an element and its ref.

text.description: Plain text to search for in the page snapshot (case-insensitive substring match). Provide either text or regex, not both.

regex.description: Regular expression to search for in the page snapshot. Matching is case-sensitive by default; wrap the pattern in slashes to add flags, e.g. "/error/i" for case-insensitive. Provide either text or regex, not both.

maxResults.description: Maximum number of matching items to return. Defaults to returning all matches.

filename.description: Save results to a file instead of returning them in the response. Relative file names are resolved against the workspace root.

playwright.name: mcp_playwright_browser_fill_form
playwright.description: [playwright] Fill multiple form fields

element.description: Human-readable element description used to obtain permission to interact with the element

target.description: Exact target element reference from the page snapshot, or a unique element selector

value.description: Value to fill in the field. If the field is a checkbox, the value should be `true` or `false`. If the field is a combobox, the value should be the text of the option.

playwright.name: mcp_playwright_browser_press_key
playwright.description: [playwright] Press a key on the keyboard

key.description: Name of the key to press or a character to generate, such as `ArrowLeft` or `a`

playwright.name: mcp_playwright_browser_type
playwright.description: [playwright] Type text into editable element

element.description: Human-readable element description used to obtain permission to interact with the element

target.description: Exact target element reference from the page snapshot, or a unique element selector

text.description: Text to type into the element

submit.description: Whether to submit entered text (press Enter after)

slowly.description: Whether to type one character at a time. Useful for triggering key handlers in the page. By default entire text is filled in at once.

playwright.name: mcp_playwright_browser_navigate
playwright.description: [playwright] Navigate to a URL

playwright.name: mcp_playwright_browser_navigate_back
playwright.description: [playwright] Go back to the previous page in the history

playwright.name: mcp_playwright_browser_network_requests
playwright.description: [playwright] Returns a numbered list of network requests since loading the page. Use browser_network_request with the number to get full details.

static.description: Whether to include successful static resources like images, fonts, scripts, etc. Defaults to false.

filter.description: Only return requests whose URL matches this regexp (e.g. "/api/.*user").

all.description: Return all network requests since the beginning of the session, not just since the last navigation. Defaults to false.

filename.description: File name to save the network requests to. Relative file names are resolved against the workspace root. If not provided, requests are returned as text.

playwright.name: mcp_playwright_browser_network_request
playwright.description: [playwright] Returns full details (headers and body) of a single network request, or a single part if `part` is set. Use the number from browser_network_requests.

index.description: 1-based index of the request, as printed by browser_network_requests.

part.description: Return only this part of the request. Omit to return full details.

filename.description: File name to save the result to. Relative file names are resolved against the workspace root. If not provided, output is returned as text.

playwright.name: mcp_playwright_browser_run_code_unsafe
playwright.description: [playwright] Run a Playwright code snippet. Unsafe: executes arbitrary JavaScript in the Playwright server process and is RCE-equivalent.

code.description: A JavaScript function containing Playwright code to execute. It will be invoked with a single argument, page, which you can use for any page interaction. For example: `async (page) => { await page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Submit' }).click(); return await page.title(); }`

filename.description: Load code from the specified file. Relative file names are resolved against the workspace root. If both code and filename are provided, code will be ignored.

playwright.name: mcp_playwright_browser_take_screenshot
playwright.description: [playwright] Take a screenshot of the current page. You can't perform actions based on the screenshot, use browser_snapshot for actions.

element.description: Human-readable element description used to obtain permission to interact with the element

target.description: Exact target element reference from the page snapshot, or a unique element selector

type.description: Image format for the screenshot. If unset, inferred from the filename extension, otherwise png.

filename.description: File name to save the screenshot to. Relative file names are resolved against the workspace root. If not specified, the screenshot is saved into the output directory as `page-{timestamp}.{png|jpeg|webp}`.

fullPage.description: When true, takes a screenshot of the full scrollable page, instead of the currently visible viewport. Cannot be used with element screenshots.

scale.description: Image resolution scale. "css" produces a screenshot sized in CSS pixels (smaller, consistent across devices). "device" produces a high-resolution screenshot using device pixels (larger, accounts for the device pixel ratio). Default is css.

playwright.name: mcp_playwright_browser_snapshot
playwright.description: [playwright] Capture accessibility snapshot of the current page, this is better than screenshot

target.description: Exact target element reference from the page snapshot, or a unique element selector

filename.description: Save snapshot to a file instead of returning it in the response. Relative file names are resolved against the workspace root.

depth.description: Limit the depth of the snapshot tree

boxes.description: Include each element's bounding box as [box=x,y,width,height] in the snapshot. Coordinates are viewport-relative, in CSS pixels (Element.getBoundingClientRect)

playwright.name: mcp_playwright_browser_click
playwright.description: [playwright] Perform click on a web page

element.description: Human-readable element description used to obtain permission to interact with the element

target.description: Exact target element reference from the page snapshot, or a unique element selector

doubleClick.description: Whether to perform a double click instead of a single click

button.description: Button to click, defaults to left

playwright.name: mcp_playwright_browser_drag
playwright.description: [playwright] Perform drag and drop between two elements

startElement.description: Human-readable source element description used to obtain the permission to interact with the element

startTarget.description: Exact target element reference from the page snapshot, or a unique element selector

endElement.description: Human-readable target element description used to obtain the permission to interact with the element

endTarget.description: Exact target element reference from the page snapshot, or a unique element selector

playwright.name: mcp_playwright_browser_hover
playwright.description: [playwright] Hover over element on page

element.description: Human-readable element description used to obtain permission to interact with the element

target.description: Exact target element reference from the page snapshot, or a unique element selector

playwright.name: mcp_playwright_browser_select_option
playwright.description: [playwright] Select an option in a dropdown

element.description: Human-readable element description used to obtain permission to interact with the element

target.description: Exact target element reference from the page snapshot, or a unique element selector

values.description: Array of values to select in the dropdown. This can be a single value or multiple values.

playwright.name: mcp_playwright_browser_tabs
playwright.description: [playwright] List, create, close, or select a browser tab.

index.description: Tab index, used for close/select. If omitted for close, current tab is closed.

url.description: URL to navigate to in the new tab, used for new.

isolatedContext.description: Name of an isolated browser context to create the new tab in, used for new. Tabs in the same isolated context share cookies and storage, tabs in different contexts are fully isolated. If omitted or "default", the tab is created in the default context.

playwright.name: mcp_playwright_browser_wait_for
playwright.description: [playwright] Wait for text to appear or disappear or a specified time to pass. When both text and textGone are provided, waits for the first one to happen

time.description: The time to wait in seconds, at most 30. When combined with text or textGone, serves as a timeout for them instead of the default action timeout

textGone.description: The text to wait for to disappear

filesystem.name: mcp_filesystem_read_file
filesystem.description: [filesystem] Read the complete contents of a file as text. DEPRECATED: Use read_text_file instead.

tail.description: If provided, returns only the last N lines of the file

head.description: If provided, returns only the first N lines of the file

filesystem.name: mcp_filesystem_read_text_file
filesystem.description: [filesystem] Read the complete contents of a file from the file system as text. Handles various text encodings and provides detailed error messages if the file cannot be read. Use this tool when you need to examine the contents of a single file. Use the 'head' parameter to read only the first N lines of a file, or the 'tail' parameter to read only the last N lines of a file. Operates on the file as text regardless of extension. Only works within allowed directories.

tail.description: If provided, returns only the last N lines of the file

head.description: If provided, returns only the first N lines of the file

filesystem.name: mcp_filesystem_read_media_file
filesystem.description: [filesystem] Read a file and return it as a base64-encoded content block with its MIME type. Image and audio files are returned as image/audio content; any other file type is returned as an embedded resource. Only works within allowed directories.

filesystem.name: mcp_filesystem_read_multiple_files
filesystem.description: [filesystem] Read the contents of multiple files simultaneously. This is more efficient than reading files one by one when you need to analyze or compare multiple files. Each file's content is returned with its path as a reference. Failed reads for individual files won't stop the entire operation. Only works within allowed directories.

paths.description: Array of file paths to read. Each path must be a string pointing to a valid file within allowed directories.

filesystem.name: mcp_filesystem_write_file
filesystem.description: [filesystem] Create a new file or completely overwrite an existing file with new content. Use with caution as it will overwrite existing files without warning. Handles text content with proper encoding. Only works within allowed directories.

filesystem.name: mcp_filesystem_edit_file
filesystem.description: [filesystem] Make line-based edits to a text file. Each edit replaces exact line sequences with new content. Returns a git-style diff showing the changes made. Only works within allowed directories.

oldText.description: Text to search for - must match exactly

dryRun.description: Preview changes using git-style diff format

filesystem.name: mcp_filesystem_create_directory
filesystem.description: [filesystem] Create a new directory or ensure a directory exists. Can create multiple nested directories in one operation. If the directory already exists, this operation will succeed silently. Perfect for setting up directory structures for projects or ensuring required paths exist. Only works within allowed directories.

filesystem.name: mcp_filesystem_list_directory
filesystem.description: [filesystem] Get a detailed listing of all files and directories in a specified path. Results clearly distinguish between files and directories with [FILE] and [DIR] prefixes. This tool is essential for understanding directory structure and finding specific files within a directory. Only works within allowed directories.

filesystem.name: mcp_filesystem_list_directory_with_sizes
filesystem.description: [filesystem] Get a detailed listing of all files and directories in a specified path, including sizes. Results clearly distinguish between files and directories with [FILE] and [DIR] prefixes. This tool is useful for understanding directory structure and finding specific files within a directory. Only works within allowed directories.

sortBy.description: Sort entries by name or size

filesystem.name: mcp_filesystem_directory_tree
filesystem.description: [filesystem] Get a recursive tree view of files and directories as a JSON structure. Each entry includes 'name', 'type' (file/directory), and 'children' for directories. Files have no children array, while directories always have a children array (which may be empty). The output is formatted with 2-space indentation for readability. Only works within allowed directories.

filesystem.name: mcp_filesystem_move_file
filesystem.description: [filesystem] Move or rename files and directories. Can move files between directories and rename them in a single operation. If the destination exists, the operation will fail. Works across different directories and can be used for simple renaming within the same directory. Both source and destination must be within allowed directories.

filesystem.name: mcp_filesystem_search_files
filesystem.description: [filesystem] Recursively search for files and directories matching a pattern. The patterns should be glob-style patterns that match paths relative to the working directory. Use pattern like '*.ext' to match files in current directory, and '**/*.ext' to match files in all subdirectories. Returns full paths to all matching items. Great for finding files when you don't know their exact location. Only searches within allowed directories.

filesystem.name: mcp_filesystem_get_file_info
filesystem.description: [filesystem] Retrieve detailed metadata about a file or directory. Returns comprehensive information including size, creation time, last modified time, permissions, type and hard-link count. This tool is perfect for understanding file characteristics without reading the actual content. Only works within allowed directories.

filesystem.name: mcp_filesystem_list_allowed_directories
filesystem.description: [filesystem] Returns the list of directories that this server is allowed to access. Subdirectories within these allowed directories are also accessible. Use this to understand which directories and their nested paths are available before trying to access files.

memory.name: mcp_memory_create_entities
memory.description: [memory] Create multiple new entities in the knowledge graph. An entity whose name already exists, or repeats an earlier entity in the same call, is skipped and its observations are not added; the result lists the skipped names in `skipped`. Use add_observations to add observations to an existing entity.

observations.description: An array of observation contents associated with the entity

memory.name: mcp_memory_create_relations
memory.description: [memory] Create multiple new relations between entities in the knowledge graph. Relations should be in active voice

from.description: The name of the entity where the relation starts

to.description: The name of the entity where the relation ends

memory.name: mcp_memory_add_observations
memory.description: [memory] Add new observations to existing entities in the knowledge graph

entityName.description: The name of the entity to add the observations to

contents.description: An array of observation contents to add

memory.name: mcp_memory_delete_entities
memory.description: [memory] Delete multiple entities and their associated relations from the knowledge graph

entityNames.description: An array of entity names to delete

memory.name: mcp_memory_delete_observations
memory.description: [memory] Delete specific observations from entities in the knowledge graph

entityName.description: The name of the entity containing the observations

observations.description: An array of observations to delete

memory.name: mcp_memory_delete_relations
memory.description: [memory] Delete multiple relations from the knowledge graph

from.description: The name of the entity where the relation starts

to.description: The name of the entity where the relation ends

relations.description: An array of relations to delete

memory.name: mcp_memory_search_nodes
memory.description: [memory] Search for nodes in the knowledge graph based on a query

query.description: The search query to match against entity names, types, and observation content

memory.name: mcp_memory_open_nodes
memory.description: [memory] Open specific nodes in the knowledge graph by their names

names.description: An array of entity names to retrieve
